docs.text: Administrators Family and player logins can never hold admin roles. Family credentials are shared within the household. The search won't offer them and the server refuses them — this is deliberate, not a bug. How do I add a brand-new administrator who has no account? Have them register on this job's site as a coach/staff adult — that creates a personal account. They'll then show up in this screen's search badged Pending adult . Accept them with the role you want; their pending registration is converted into the admin registration and they leave the coach-approval queue automatically. Why can't I find the person I'm searching for? The search is scoped to the role you selected — it only offers accounts that have only ever held that role (Director and SuperDirector count together), plus pending coach/staff adults registered with this customer. If the person's account has any other role anywhere — family, player, referee, coach — they won't appear; have them create a fresh coach/staff account on this site instead. If they registered with a different customer, they need to register on this site. Why can't I make our referee a Ref Assignor (or our Director a Store Admin)? Deliberate: no cross-type grants . Each admin role is granted only to accounts that have never held any other role, so every login means exactly one thing from a security point of view. When a person takes on a new kind of role, they register a fresh coach/staff adult account on this site and get accepted into the new role with it — one account per hat. A parent should be our new Director. Can I use their family account? No — and the screen will refuse it. Their family login stays with the household (the kids may know the password). Have the parent register on the site as a coach/staff adult with their own username and email, then accept that account here. Two logins, cleanly separated lives. What happens to their coach registration when I accept a Pending adult? It becomes the admin registration — same row, converted in place. They drop out of the coach-approval queue and won't be granted teams as a coach. If someone should genuinely be both a coach and an admin, talk it through first: those are two different access lives and usually deserve two accounts. What does the star do? Marks the job's primary contact — the Director published as the event's point of contact. One per job, and never empty: the earliest-registered active Director holds it by default. Click another active Director's star to hand it over; click the starred row to revert to the default. Should I deactivate or delete a departing admin? Deactivate if they might return (between seasons) — the row stays, access stops. Delete when they're gone for good. Either way, do it promptly — stale admin access is the easiest thing to forget and the most expensive to leave open.

docs.text: Administrators This screen controls who can run this job — Directors, SuperDirectors, and the other admin roles. Every row is a real person with access to the job's sensitive data: player and family contact information, medical forms, payments, and accounting. Adding someone here is the single most powerful grant in the system, so the screen is SuperUser-only and deliberately picky about who it will accept. Each admin role is its own lane — no cross-type grants. An account is eligible for a role only if it has never held any other role , anywhere on the platform — or is a pending coach/staff adult registered with this customer. Director and SuperDirector count as one lane (two trust levels of the same person); Ref Assignor, Store Admin, STPAdmin, and ApiAuthorized are each strictly their own. Family and player logins never qualify for anything — family credentials are shared within a household, and elevating one would hand admin access to everyone who knows the password, including the kids. Adding an existing admin Add Administrator → pick the role first — the search only looks inside that role's lane. Accounts badged Admin account already hold exactly this role (or its Director/SuperDirector sibling) elsewhere; selecting one pins them to this job with a new admin registration. A Director cannot be handed Store Admin, and a referee's account cannot become Ref Assignor — people wearing a new hat come through the funnel below with a fresh account. Adding a brand-new person Someone who has never held an admin role needs their own account first — never a shared family login. The path: 1. They register as a coach/staff adult on this job's site (the adult registration flow), creating a personal account. 2. They appear in this screen's search badged Pending adult . 3. You accept them with the admin role you want. Their pending coach/staff registration is converted into the admin registration — one account, one registration, and they drop out of the coach-approval queue automatically. Roles Director — full admin for this job. SuperDirector — Director plus cross-job powers within the customer. Ref Assignor / Store Admin / STPAdmin — scoped admin roles for refereeing, the store, and STP. ApiAuthorized — an export-only login for an outside organization you've agreed to share rosters with. It is not an admin: signing in shows a single menu item, the Authorized Rosters and Schedule Export , and nothing else on the site. Before you add an ApiAuthorized login, decide what it may see. The export ships rosters for only the age groups where you've turned on Third-Party Roster Access (Teams & Rosters → L-A-D-T Editor). No age groups enabled means the file downloads with no roster data. The setting is per event and is never inherited — cloning a job leaves it off on purpose. Schedules are public information and are included in full. Give this role only to an organization you have a relationship with; the data is minors' contact information and it leaves your control once it's downloaded. Primary contact The star marks the job's primary contact — the Director whose name goes out as the event's public point of contact. Every job has one: by default it's the earliest-registered active Director , set automatically. Click another active Director's star to hand it to them; click the starred row to revert to the default. Active / Inactive The status toggle suspends an admin without deleting them — useful between seasons. Activate All / Deactivate All act on every non-SuperUser row at once. Common mistakes Trying to add a parent's family login. It won't be offered, and the server will refuse it. If a parent should be a Director, have them create their own coach/staff account on the site first — the household keeps its family login for the kids, and the admin role rides on personal credentials. Expecting a just-registered coach to keep their coach spot. Accepting a Pending adult here converts that registration to the admin role — it's an either/or, not both.

docs.text: Adult Registration — questions Does picking teams add me to a roster? No. Choosing teams as a coach is a request — it doesn't place you on a roster or give you roster access. A director reviews and approves coach assignments first. Until then you're treated as unassigned. Do I have to verify my USA Lacrosse membership? No — it's optional. If you can't get the emailed code, choose "continue without verifying" and a director will verify you before you're assigned. Verifying now just saves that step later. The code never arrived. It goes to the email USA Lacrosse has on file, not necessarily the one on your event account — the screen shows a masked hint of where it was sent. Check spam, or continue without verifying and let a director handle it. My card was declined — am I registered? Yes. Your registration is saved and no charge was made; a balance stays owing. Sign back in with the account you just created to pay it, or ask the event director for help. Can I pay by check instead of card? When a fee is owed, the Payment step offers Pay by Check . Your registration is recorded right away and confirmed once your mailed check is received. Why can't I change my name? Once your account exists, your name is locked on the profile step. To correct it, contact the tournament director. It says "Registration Unavailable." The link you opened is missing its role, so the wizard can't tell what you're registering as. Ask the event director for the correct registration link. Why don't I see a Payment step? Because there's no fee owed for your role at this event. When nothing's due, the wizard submits your registration straight from the Review step. I didn't get my confirmation email. On the final step, use Resend Confirmation Email . If it still doesn't arrive, check spam and confirm your email on the account is correct.

docs.text: Adult Registration This wizard registers you for the event as an adult — a coach, referee, or recruiter. It walks you through signing in, filling out a short profile, accepting any waivers, and paying any fee. Your role comes from the link you followed, so the questions you're asked are tailored to it. The steps Account Profile Waivers Review Payment Done Account — sign in, or create a new account. Coming back from the User Menu, you're signed in and dropped straight onto your profile. Profile — the details for your role. Names are locked once your account exists (contact the director to change one). Waivers — read and check each required agreement. This step is skipped when the event has none. Review — one last look at everything, including any fees. Payment — appears only when a fee is owed. Pay by card, or choose pay-by-check. Done — your confirmation, with a button to resend the email. Coaches: requesting teams If you're registering as a coach, your profile may let you pick the teams you'd like to coach. This is a request only — it does not add you to a roster or grant roster access. A director reviews and approves coach assignments before you can see any roster. Coaches: USA Lacrosse verification Where the event asks for it, enter your USA Lacrosse number and choose Verify my USA Lacrosse membership . A 6-digit code is emailed to the address USA Lacrosse has on file; enter it to confirm. Can't reach that inbox? You can continue without verifying — a director will verify you before you're assigned. If your card is declined, you're still registered. Your registration is saved and a balance stays owing — no charge was made. Sign back in with the account you just created to pay it, or contact the event director. "Registration Unavailable"? That means the link you opened is missing its role. Ask the event director for the correct registration link for your role.

docs.title: Age Ranges
headings: Age Ranges
What is an age range, exactly?
A player was accepted (or rejected) for the wrong age group. Why?
Can ranges overlap?
Do I always need to set these up?
Is renaming a range enough to change who qualifies?
docs.text: Age Ranges The birthdate window is what enforces eligibility — not the name. "U12" only means what its DOB From/To say. Get those dates right against your official age cutoffs. What is an age range, exactly? A named eligibility band with a birthdate window — a Range Name (U12, U14, Open) plus a DOB From and DOB To . A player qualifies for the range when their birthdate falls inside that window. A player was accepted (or rejected) for the wrong age group. Why? Almost always the range's DOB From/To dates. Eligibility is decided by that window, so an off-by-one boundary admits over-age players or turns away ones who should qualify. Check the dates against your governing body's cutoff for the season. Can ranges overlap? Avoid it. If two ranges cover the same birthdate, it's ambiguous which age group a player belongs to. Keep each range's window distinct so every birthdate maps cleanly to one band. Do I always need to set these up? Only when your event uses age-based team eligibility. If the event doesn't gate by age, age ranges don't apply and you can leave them alone. Is renaming a range enough to change who qualifies? No — the name is just a label. To change who's eligible you have to change the DOB From/To window. A range renamed without adjusting its dates still admits exactly the same players. Tip: set your age ranges from your governing body's published cutoff dates for the season, and re-check them each year — the birthdate boundaries shift as the season rolls forward.

docs.text: Age Ranges Age ranges define who is eligible for each age group by birthdate. Each range is a named band — like U12 , U14 , or Open — with a date-of-birth window. When a family registers, their player's birthdate is checked against these ranges to confirm they fit the age group they're signing up for. A range is a name plus a birthdate window. "U12" isn't just a label here — it's a DOB From and DOB To that decide exactly who qualifies. What each range holds Range Name — the label players and admins see (e.g. U12, U14, Open). DOB From / DOB To — the earliest and latest birthdate that qualifies for the range. Add, edit, or remove ranges as your event's divisions require. Getting the dates right The birthdate window is the whole point — set it to your governing body's cutoff rules for the season. A range that's too wide lets over-age players in; too narrow turns away players who should qualify. Double-check the DOB From and DOB To against the official age cutoffs before you rely on them. When you'll see this Age ranges apply when an event uses age-based team eligibility . If your event doesn't gate by age, you won't need to configure them. Common mistakes Off-by-a-year windows. Age cutoffs are unforgiving — a DOB boundary one day or one year off admits or rejects the wrong players. Overlapping ranges. If two ranges cover the same birthdate, eligibility gets ambiguous. Keep the windows clean and non-overlapping. Naming without dating. The name is cosmetic; the DOB window does the work. A correctly-named range with the wrong dates still lets the wrong players in.

docs.text: ARB Subscription Health Timing is everything on the Expiring Cards lookup. A card flagged as expiring hasn't failed yet — you have a window to get it updated before the next automatic charge. Act early in the month, not after the decline. What does ARB stand for? Automatic Recurrent Billing — the installment payment plans families sign up for. This page monitors the health of those plans and flags the ones at risk of failing. Why is the page empty when I open it? By design. Nothing loads until you click a lookup button, so opening the page never fires off work you didn't ask for. Choose Lookup Behind in Payment or Lookup Expiring Cards to fill the grid. What's the difference between the two lookups? Expiring Cards is preventive — the card on file expires this month and the next charge will fail if it isn't updated. Behind in Payment is corrective — a charge already declined and the family now owes a balance. One is "fix it before," the other "fix it after." What does "Refresh ARB Statuses" actually do? It walks every subscription in the job, asks Authorize.Net for its current status, and stores the answer. That stored status is what the Behind in Payment lookup reads, so a refresh is what makes that list trustworthy. It's read-only at Authorize.Net — it can't charge, change, or cancel anything. Run it at the start of a working session. On a big job it takes a while, since it checks one subscription at a time. The refresh says "Checked 120 · updated 4 · 2 failed" — what's a failure? Checked is how many subscriptions were looked at, updated how many had changed status since last time, and failed how many Authorize.Net didn't answer for. A couple of failures is normally a transient hiccup — those subscriptions simply keep their previous stored status and get picked up on the next refresh. A refresh where everything fails points at an Authorize.Net credential problem for the job, not at the families. What's the difference between "Owes Now" and "Owes Total"? Owes Total is everything still outstanding on the registration, including installments that aren't due yet. Owes Now is only the part that is past due today by the installment schedule — the amount you can fairly ask a family for right now. The collection templates quote Owes Now via the !OWEDNOW token. Why does "Owes Now" read $0.00 on the Expiring Cards list? Because nothing has failed yet. An expiring card is a warning about the next charge, not a missed one — so there's no past-due amount to show. If that family also has a genuine arrears balance, they'll turn up on the Behind in Payment lookup with a real figure. A family I know is behind isn't on the list. Why? Three common reasons, all deliberate: 48-hour grace. If their scheduled payment date was less than two days ago, they're held back — the charge may still be settling, and nobody wants a dunning email over a payment that's about to post. Canceled subscriptions are skipped. A canceled plan isn't a billing failure to chase here; handle that balance through the registrant's accounting. Stale status. Click Refresh ARB Statuses and run the lookup again. Which email template should I pick? Match it to the Status column. Active/Suspended Subscriptions sends them to "Update CC Info", which repairs the card and clears the failed payments in one step — that only works while a subscription still exists. Expired/Terminated Subscriptions sends them to "Pay Balance Due" instead, because there's no live plan left to fix. If your selection mixes both kinds, send in two passes — one template per group. Is there help for parents, and where do I send them? Yes. Most of the time you won't need to send them anywhere — the email templates on this page already carry the step-by-step instructions to the parent. Reach for the help page when someone phones you. Families have their own written help in two places, both behind the ? button: The Update Payment Method screen For a parent already on the page The player registration screens For a parent who doesn't know where to start Between them they cover: Signing in, choosing the player's role, and finding Update CC Info in the User Menu. What Balance Due at the top of the form means — zero is up to date, anything else is charged when they submit. That updating the card and paying a missed installment are the same single step. That each player carries their own card, so a family with two players repeats it under Switch Role . Browser, device, and firewall troubleshooting when the form won't go through. The call you'll actually get: "I don't see Update CC Info." That item only appears for a player who is on an automatic-payment plan. Nine times out of ten the parent is signed in under a different player — have them use Switch Role and look again. Can I edit a template before sending? Yes — applying a template just pre-fills the subject and body, and both are fully editable. Keep the numbered login steps intact, though: they're the part families actually act on. What are the tokens like !PLAYER and !OWEDNOW? Personalization placeholders. When the email goes out, each token is replaced with that recipient's real value. Click one to insert it at your cursor. The full set: !PLAYER — the player's name ( !PERSON works too, if that's the habit you have from the Search composer) !FAMILYUSERNAME — the username the family logs in with !JOBLINK — the event name as a clickable link; !JOBNAME for the name alone !OWEDNOW — past-due amount; !OWEDTOTAL — full remaining balance !FEETOTAL and !PAIDTOTAL — total fees and total paid !SUBSCRIPTIONID and !SUBSCRIPTIONSTATUS — the Authorize.Net subscription details What does "email a summary to job directors" send? One recap message to the job's directors listing the families that were contacted — not a copy of each individual email, and not a BCC. Leave it on so staff have a record of the outreach; turn it off only for a deliberately quiet send. The one-click "Send Warning to All" — who gets it? Everyone currently listed on the Expiring Cards lookup, plus a summary to directors, using the standard expiration notice. It's all-or-nothing by design — that list is the routine monthly warning. There's no per-recipient selection or custom wording on that side; if you need to say something different, contact the family directly using the links in the Contact column. What happens after I click Send? The batch runs in the background and the button stays busy until it's done. You then get a summary — how many sent, how many failed, and the specific addresses that failed. A failed address usually means a bad or blocked email; the E-Mail Troubleshooter page will tell you which. Why is the family username shown on every row? Because "which username do I log in with?" is the question that stalls these fixes. Every template quotes it back to the family automatically, and having it on the row means you can answer a phone call without digging. Clicking a row selects it — how do I just email or call a parent? Click the email address or phone number itself in the Contact column. Those links open your mail or phone app and deliberately don't toggle the row's checkbox, so your selection stays intact. Tip: make ARB Health a monthly habit — refresh statuses, run Expiring Cards near the start of the month, then run Behind in Payment. A few minutes there prevents most of the declines you'd otherwise be chasing later.

docs.text: ARB Subscription Health ARB Health watches over your event's Automatic Recurrent Billing — the families paying by installment plan. It surfaces the two things that break those payment plans before they cost you money: cards that are about to expire, and payments that have already been declined. From here you can email the affected families a ready-made message telling them exactly how to fix it. This is your safety net for recurring revenue. Every registrant on this page is one failed charge away from a gap in payment. Working the list keeps installment plans on track instead of quietly lapsing. Refresh statuses Run a lookup Review the list Email the families The page opens empty — that's on purpose Nothing loads until you ask for it. Two buttons run the lookups: Lookup Behind in Payment — families whose automatic payment was already declined and who now owe a balance. They need to update their card and clear what's due. This reads the subscription statuses already stored for your job, so it comes back quickly. Lookup Expiring Cards — families whose card on file expires this month . Their next automatic payment will fail unless they update the card first. This one queries Authorize.Net live, so give it a moment. Clicking the lookup you're already on re-runs it — that's how you refresh the list after sending emails or after a family fixes their card. Refresh ARB Statuses The button at the top of the page re-checks every subscription in the job against Authorize.Net and writes back the current status (active, suspended, expired, terminated, canceled). It's the one place those stored statuses get synced, and the Behind in Payment lookup is only as accurate as the last refresh. Click it before your first lookup of the session so you're working from live status. On a large job it can take a while — it checks one subscription at a time. Let it finish. It reports Checked · updated · failed . "Updated" means the status changed since last time; "failed" means Authorize.Net didn't answer for that subscription — usually harmless, and the next refresh picks it up. If a lookup was already on screen, the refresh reloads it automatically. If not, it leaves the page neutral — refreshing never runs a lookup for you. Reading the list Registrant — name, team/assignment, and the Family Username . That username is what the family logs in with, and the email templates quote it back to them, so it's the single most useful thing on the row when someone calls confused. Status — the stored Authorize.Net subscription status. Green = active, amber = suspended, red = anything else (expired, terminated, unknown). Fee Total and Paid — what the registration costs and what's come in so far. Owes Total — the full remaining balance on the registration. Owes Now — the part that is past due today based on the installment schedule. This is the number the collection templates quote. It shows red when it's above zero. Next Payment and Progress — when the next installment is scheduled and how far through the plan they are (for example, "3 of 6"). Contact — the player's email plus both parent contacts. Emails and phone numbers are clickable; clicking one opens your mail or phone app without disturbing the row's checkbox. Emailing flagged families The two lookups deliberately work differently: Expiring Cards is one click: Send Warning to All Registrants & Directors sends the standard expiration notice to everyone on the list. There's nothing to select and nothing to compose — it's the routine monthly warning. Behind in Payment is select-and-compose, because collections messages usually need a human touch. Select the registrants to contact — click anywhere on a row, or use the header checkbox to take the whole list. Click Compose Email , then apply a template . Pick the one that matches the subscription status: Active/Suspended Subscriptions — points them at "Update CC Info", which updates the card and clears the failed payments in one step. Expired/Terminated Subscriptions — points them at "Pay Balance Due", because there's no live subscription left to repair. Edit the subject and body freely — the template is a starting point, not a locked form. Insert tokens where you want per-family values: !PLAYER , !OWEDNOW , !OWEDTOTAL , !FAMILYUSERNAME , !JOBLINK , and more. Click a token to drop it at your cursor. Leave "Email a summary to job directors" checked to send staff a record of who was contacted, then Send to N recipient(s) . Sending runs in the background; a summary appears when it finishes, listing any addresses that failed. Common mistakes Working a stale list. Refresh ARB Statuses first — otherwise Behind in Payment reflects whatever the statuses were the last time anyone synced. Waiting until payments fail. Run Expiring Cards early in the month — the whole point is to fix the card before the charge bounces. Editing the fix-it steps out of the template. The numbered login steps are how families actually resolve it; keep them intact. Sending with nothing selected. On Behind in Payment, emails go only to the rows you've checked — the Send button counts them for you, so confirm the count before you click. Picking the wrong template. Telling a family with a terminated subscription to "update CC info" sends them looking for a menu item they no longer have.

docs.text: Update Payment Method — questions I missed an installment — how do I pay it? Right here. There's no separate screen for a missed payment: the Balance Due at the top of this page is the past-due amount, and Update Card & Pay Balance charges it while storing your new card. Balance Due 0.00 — you're up to date. Nothing is charged now; the card is saved for future installments. Any other amount — that's what the button will charge today. You can enter the same card you already had on file if it's working again — the charge goes through either way. Your installment schedule and amounts don't change. This page is for a plan that's still running. If your automatic payments have been cancelled or have come to an end, there's no card on file left to update. Use Pay Balance Due in the User Menu instead — it takes a card and settles what's owed in a single payment. I have more than one player. Does this cover all of them? No — each player's automatic-payment plan holds its own card, so you'll need to repeat this for each one. Open the User Menu in the upper right, choose Switch Role , select your next player, and come back to Update CC Info . Update CC Info Switch Role Pick your next player, then repeat Before entering card details, check that the player name and event shown at the top of this page are the ones you meant to pay for. Will this charge my card right now? Yes — updating the card also pays the Balance Due shown at the top. If that figure is zero, no charge is made; the page just stores your new card for future drafts. Does this change my payment schedule or amounts? No. It only swaps the card on file and settles today's balance. The plan's timing and installment amounts stay exactly as they were. Why is the Update button greyed out? Every field is required. Fill in all of the cardholder and card details — name, address, ZIP, email, card number, CVV, and expiration month and year — and the button becomes active. The page says it couldn't load my subscription. The link may be invalid or expired, or it's missing its registration reference. Open it again from the Update CC Info item in your User Menu, or contact the event director for a fresh link. The update failed — what now? You'll see the reason on screen (for example, the card was declined). Double-check the card number, expiration, and CVV, then try again — or use a different card. If the card is definitely good and the page still won't complete, it's usually the device or network: Try a different browser. Try a different device — if you're on a phone, try a computer. Avoid school or work devices; their firewalls frequently block payment forms. How do I get a receipt? Enter the email you'd like the receipt sent to in the cardholder section. On success the page also shows the amount charged and a transaction reference for your records.

docs.title: Update Payment Method
headings: Update Payment Method
Your plan at a glance
What you enter
docs.text: Update Payment Method You're on a payment plan for this event — your balance is drafted automatically from a card we keep on file. This page lets you replace that card and settle the current balance in one step, so an expired or changed card doesn't cause a missed draft. Your plan at a glance At the top you'll see a summary of your plan: your name, the event, your subscription reference, and the current Balance Due . That's the amount this page will charge to the new card. What you enter Cardholder Information First and last name, billing address, ZIP, and an email for the receipt. Card Details Card number, CVV, and the expiration month and year. All fields are required, so the Update Card & Pay Balance button stays disabled until the form is complete. Choosing it saves the new card as your plan's card and charges the balance shown. You'll get a clear result. On success the page confirms your card was updated and shows the amount charged (with a transaction reference). If something goes wrong, it tells you the reason so you can retry. Future drafts use the new card. From here on, your plan draws from the card you just entered. This page doesn't change your plan's schedule or amounts — only the card behind it and today's balance.

docs.text: Bracket Seeds You assign a pool and a rank — not a team. The actual team is resolved from final standings. That's the one idea that makes this whole screen click. Why can't I pick the actual teams for a playoff game? Because at seeding time you usually don't know them yet — pool play isn't finished. You set a Seed Pool and a Seed Rank (e.g. "Pool A, Seed 1"), and once standings are final the bracket automatically pulls in whichever team earned that spot. The page says there are no bracket games. Where are they? Bracket/playoff games are created during scheduling , as non-round-robin game types (championship, final, semi, quarter). This screen only seeds games that already exist. If the list is empty, build the schedule first, then come back to seed it. A game's side says "Fed" and won't let me seed it. Why? That slot is filled by the winner of an earlier bracket game , so there's no seed to assign — the team advances in on results. Only slots that come out of pool play take a seed. Games where every slot is fed (finals, most semis) don't appear on this page at all: if a game is listed, at least one of its sides needs you. Every dash you see on a seedable side is therefore a real gap — fill them all and the checklist's Bracket Seeds step goes green. Where do I find this screen? As step 5 of the Scheduling Checklist — it appears there once the event has bracket games. The arrow beside the title takes you back to the checklist. What does "Pool A #1 plays Pool B #2" actually mean? Each game has two sides. One side is set to Pool A, rank 1; the other to Pool B, rank 2. So the winner of Pool A meets the runner-up of Pool B. You're describing the matchup by finishing position , and the teams drop in from standings. How do I know I've seeded it correctly? Use the Standings panel on this page. It shows each pool's order — record, points, goal differential. Cross-check that the seeds you assigned match the way you expect the pools to finish, so no slot is left pointing at a rank that pool can't produce. Can I change a seed after games have been played? You can, but be deliberate — a seed drives who advances into that game. After any change, re-check the affected bracket games so a downstream matchup doesn't end up pointing at the wrong pool or rank. This event says "Re-seed mode." What's different? On a re-seed event, a seed pool can be drawn from any round-robin age group across the job, not just this game's own age group — and each side's available ranks are capped at the size of the pool you choose. The banner at the top flags when you're in that mode. Tip: seed the bracket before pool play ends. Because slots resolve from standings, a fully-seeded bracket simply fills itself in the moment the last pool game is scored — no scramble on finals morning.

docs.text: Bracket Seeds This screen defines the playoff bracket — which teams feed each championship game. You don't pick team names here. Instead, each game slot is filled by a seed : a pool plus a rank, like "the #1 team out of Pool A." When pool play finishes, standings decide who that actually is, and the bracket fills itself in. You're wiring the bracket, not choosing teams. A slot set to "Pool A, Seed 1" resolves to whichever team finishes first in Pool A — automatically, from the standings. How a bracket game is defined Every bracket/playoff game has two sides. For each side you set two things: Seed Pool Which round-robin pool (division/age group) the team comes from. Seed Rank Where they finished in that pool — 1 for the winner, 2 for runner-up, and so on. Read together, the two sides of a game say something like "Pool A #1 plays Pool B #2." Click Edit on a game to set its two seeds. Not every slot needs a seed — some are fed. A first-round slot comes out of pool play, so it needs a seed. A semi-final or final slot is filled by the winner of an earlier bracket game — it never needs seeding. This page only lists games with at least one slot to seed; a game whose slots are all fed (a final, a semi) doesn't appear at all, and on a listed game a fed side shows a Fed badge instead of seed fields. In a 12-team bracket that's 8 rows: the play-in games seed both sides, the quarter-finals with byes seed one. Standings are right there to guide you The Standings panel shows each pool's current order — games played, record, points. Use it to sanity-check your seeding: the seeds you assign should line up with how the standings will resolve once pool play is complete. Where do these games come from? Bracket games aren't created here — they're created during the build as non-round-robin game types (championship, final, semi, quarter, and so on). If this page says there are no bracket games, none have been created yet: build the schedule first, then come here to seed it. That's also why the checklist's Bracket Seeds step is hidden until an event actually has bracket games. Common mistakes Looking for team names. There aren't any — you assign a pool and a rank, and the team is filled in from standings later. Seeding before the bracket exists. If the list is empty, create the playoff games in scheduling first. Reseeding after games are played. Changing a seed changes who advances — only do it deliberately, and re-check the affected games. Re-seed events On a re-seed event you'll see a banner: seed pools may be drawn from any round-robin age group across the job, and each side's rank list is capped at the chosen pool's size. Everywhere else, seeding works within the event's own pools.

docs.text: Bulletins A bulletin shows only when it's active AND inside its date window. Miss either one and it stays hidden — that's the answer to almost every "why isn't my bulletin showing?" I saved a bulletin but it's not on the home page. Why? Check the two gates. The Active switch must be on, and today must be between the bulletin's Start Date and End Date . A bulletin that's inactive, or dated for next week, won't appear yet. How do I take a bulletin down? Turn its Active switch off — it stops showing immediately but stays in the list so you can reuse it later. Set an End Date if you'd rather it retire itself on a schedule. Delete only when you're sure you won't want it again. Who sees these bulletins? Anyone who visits your event's home page while the bulletin is active and in its date window. Treat them as public — they aren't private notes or targeted messages. What's the Resolved Preview and the Simulate checkboxes? The Resolved Preview renders the bulletin exactly as visitors will see it, with any tokens filled in. Because some content only appears under certain conditions, the Simulate checkboxes let you preview those variations without changing the real event settings. Check the preview before you save. What are tokens for? Tokens insert dynamic text into the content so a bulletin can adapt rather than being fully hand-typed. Insert one from the token bar and use the Resolved Preview to confirm it fills in the way you expect. Can it help me write the bulletin? Yes — describe what you want to announce and the editor can draft a title and content for you. It's a starting point; edit the wording and always preview before you make it active. Tip: use the End Date for time-bound notices — a check-in reminder or a weather update can retire itself automatically, so your home page never carries a stale announcement.

docs.text: Camp Groups Changes save as you make them. Picking a group from a camper's dropdown saves immediately — there's no separate Save button. If a save fails, the value snaps back and you'll see an error. What are day and night groups for? They're the sub-groups a camp uses to organize campers — think rotation groups, cabins, or session assignments. A camper can have a day group, a night group, or both, depending on how your camp runs. Why don't I see a Night (or Day) column? A column only appears when that type of group is configured for the event. If Night is missing, night groups haven't been set up — so there's nothing to assign there yet. How do I assign a lot of campers quickly? Tick the campers (or use select-all on the visible list), pick a group in the bulk control, and apply. It sets that group on everyone selected in one go — much faster than row by row for a full cabin. How do I find campers who still need a group? Turn on unassigned only . It filters the list to campers missing a group in a visible column, so what's left on screen is exactly your remaining work. Can I clear a camper's group? Yes — set their dropdown back to the blank/none option and it saves as unassigned, which puts them back in the "unassigned only" view. Tip: work one team at a time and finish it (use "unassigned only" to confirm zero remain) before moving on — it's the cleanest way to be sure no camper slipped through without a group.

docs.text: Check-In Check-in is quick and reversible. Tap to check someone in, tap Undo to reverse it — nothing here is locked, so work fast. Should I use Teams or Players mode? The screen picks a default from your event type — Teams for tournaments and leagues, Players for camps and tryouts. If that's not the view you want, switch modes at the top. Team mode checks in a whole team at once; player mode checks in individuals under a team. I checked in the wrong team/player. How do I fix it? Undo it from that row — check-in stamps a time but isn't permanent, so reversing a mistaken tap takes one click. The checked-in count updates accordingly. The camp roster is huge. How do I find one player fast? Use the search box in player mode — it filters by name, club, or school as you type, so you don't scroll a list of hundreds. Pick the player's team first, then search within it. Can I tell if a registrant still owes money at check-in? Yes — open their detail panel (the same fly-in from Registration Search) to see their information and payment status right at the table. It's the moment to catch an outstanding balance before someone heads out to play. How do I know how many have checked in? The count at the top tallies checked-in rows for the current mode — a live read on how far through arrivals you are. It updates every time you check someone in or undo. What's the roommate column I sometimes see? It's a camp-only field, shown only when players on the loaded roster actually have a roommate preference. On tournament or non-camp rosters it stays hidden so the table stays clean. Tip: before the event, decide who's running check-in and on what device. Any director-level admin can run this screen, and because it's reversible, more than one person can work arrivals at once without stepping on each other.

Undo it — check-in isn't permanent, so a mis-tap is a one-click fix. In player mode, use the search box to jump to a name, club, or school — camp rosters can run into the hundreds. If someone still owes a balance, you'll see it here before they head onto the field. Check-in is a good moment to catch an unpaid balance. If you expected a player list but see teams (or vice-versa), switch the mode at the top — it defaults to the event type but you can override it. Scrolling a huge roster. Don't — type in the search box to find the player instantly. Checking in the wrong row. Use Undo; nothing is locked in.

docs.text: Club Rosters — questions How do I set or change a uniform number? Click the player's name to open their panel, type the number in Uniform # , and choose Save . The grid updates right away. A dash in the # column just means no number has been set yet. What's the difference between Move and Delete? Move keeps the player registered and re-homes them to another of your teams. Delete removes their registration entirely and can't be undone. When in doubt, move. Why can't I pick a destination team? The Destination list shows only your other teams — never the one the player is already on. If it's empty, you only have the one team registered, so there's nowhere to move them yet. The Move button stays disabled until you've chosen a destination. I deleted a player by mistake. Deletion is final — there's no undo. The player would need to register again, or the event director can help restore the registration. That's why the trash button always asks you to confirm first. A team shows no players, or the page says no teams were found. "No players on this team" simply means nobody's been registered onto it yet. "No teams found for your club" means none of your teams have loaded — hit Refresh , and if it persists, check with the event director. My change didn't take. If a save, move, or delete fails you'll see a red message with the reason. Try again, and use Refresh to reload the latest roster before retrying. Can I resize that side panel? Yes — drag its edge to make it wider or narrower. Your chosen width is remembered the next time you open a player.

What's the difference between a requested team and an assigned team?
How do I remove one team without removing the coach?
How do I approve several coaches at once?
Why don't I see a "Grant All Requests" button?

The status chips at the top — what are they for?

docs.text: Coach Approvals A requested team is not access — approval is. Coaches sit in this queue with pending requests until you grant them. Nothing they asked for takes effect on its own. How do I actually approve a coach for a team? In the coach's Teams cell, check the team they requested — that grant is immediate. Use Grant all to approve every team they asked for at once. To put them on a team they didn't request, use Add team . What's the difference between a requested team and an assigned team? A request is what the coach asked for (marked as coming from the coach); it's still pending. An assigned team is one they currently hold because you granted it. The Teams checklist shows granted teams on top and pending requests below. How do I remove one team without removing the coach? Uncheck just that team in the Teams cell — it removes only that grant (after a quick confirm). The removed team stays listed in the cell, so you can re-grant it later — and the row becomes selectable for the batch grant buttons again. How do I approve several coaches at once? Check the selection box on the right of each row, then click Grant Requests of Checked Rows Only above the grid (it appears once something is checked) — it grants every ungranted team on those rows in one pass. The header's Select All With Requests checks every listed registrant with something to grant, and it respects the status chips and search, so filter first and you're selecting exactly who you see. Rows with nothing to grant have a muted checkbox — there's nothing to batch for them. A confirmation dialog shows the registrant and team counts before anything is written, and if one grant fails the rest still complete; the failed rows stay checked for a retry. Why don't I see a "Grant All Requests" button? Two possible reasons. If nothing in the current list has an ungranted team, the batch controls don't render at all — there's nothing for them to do. Beyond that, the button only appears when coaches & staff cannot view team rosters on this event — the "Allow coaches & staff to view their team roster" setting under Job Settings → Teams/ClubReps → Roster Visibility . With roster viewing on, every grant hands the coach the personal information of the players on those teams, so blanket granting is deliberately not offered — vet, check rows, and use Grant Requests of Checked Rows Only instead. How do I deny a coach — someone who shouldn't be on any team? Just don't grant them anything — and uncheck any team they already hold. A registrant with no granted teams has no roles on this event : no roster access, no staff messaging, nothing. There's no separate deny or deactivate button because there's nothing left to turn off; they simply stay listed under Unassigned . How do I know a coach is who they say they are? Two signals. Coached before shows their prior team/job history so you can recognize a returning coach. On lacrosse events, the Verified badge shows whether they proved ownership of their USA Lacrosse membership email at sign-up, with the membership number and expiry; Re-validate refreshes that check. The status chips at the top — what are they for? They filter the list by Unassigned vs Assigned and carry live counts, so they double as a progress meter — how many coaches still need at least one team. Picking a chip pins the visible set; granting a coach updates the counts but leaves the row in place until you re-pick a chip or refresh. Where do I move players and coaches between teams? That's the Roster Swapper , which this queue is part of. This screen is specifically the approval gate for coach requests; the Swapper handles moving people between existing teams. Tip: use the Unassigned chip as your worklist — it's every coach still waiting on a team. When that count reaches zero, everyone who registered has been reviewed.

docs.text: Coach Approvals This is the gate between "a coach signed up" and "a coach is on a team." Coaches register and request the teams they want to coach — but those requests do nothing until you approve them here. Each row is one coach; you decide which teams they actually get. Granting a team gives a real adult access to that team. Rosters, contact info, team messaging — approval is what unlocks it. Vet before you grant. Reading a coach row Status — the row's color shows whether a coach is Unassigned (holds no teams) or Assigned (holds at least one). The chips at the top filter by status and double as a live progress meter. Coached before — a popover of the coach's prior team/job history, so you can recognize a returning coach. Verified — for lacrosse events, shows whether the coach proved ownership of their USA Lacrosse membership email at sign-up, along with their membership number and expiry. Use Re-validate to refresh it. Granting and removing teams The Teams cell is the one control that does everything — it's a checklist: Check a requested team to grant it. Grant all approves every team the coach asked for at once. Add team places the coach on a team they didn't request — useful when you're assigning coaches yourself. Uncheck a granted team to remove that one grant (it asks you to confirm). Acting on a coach recolors the row in place — it won't jump or disappear under your cursor, so you can work down the list steadily. Granting in bulk For a long queue you don't have to work one row at a time. Each row has a selection checkbox on the right, and the buttons above that column act on it. A row is selectable whenever it has a recorded team that isn't currently granted — a team the coach requested, or one you removed earlier. Rows with nothing to grant have a muted checkbox, and the batch controls only appear when they have something to act on: Grant Requests of Checked Rows Only appears once you've checked at least one row, and grants every ungranted team on those rows. Checking named registrants is still per-coach vetting — just batched. Select All With Requests , in the column header, checks every listed registrant with something to grant. It follows the status chips and the search box, so it only ever selects rows you can see. Grant All Requests grants every ungranted team in the current list. This button only appears when coaches & staff cannot view team rosters on this event (Job Settings → Teams/ClubReps → Roster Visibility) — because then a grant exposes no player personal information. When roster viewing is on, a grant hands over player contact details, so it stays a coach-by-coach decision. The counts on both buttons cover only what is ungranted: teams already granted are never touched or re-sent. A confirmation dialog spells out exactly what the grant unlocks on this event before anything is written. If one grant fails, the rest of the batch still completes — the failed rows stay checked so you can retry. Declining a coach There is no separate deny button — unchecking is the whole story. A registrant holding no teams has no roles on this event: they can't see rosters, can't be messaged as staff, and simply remain listed as Unassigned . To decline someone, remove (or never grant) their teams and move on. Common mistakes Granting without vetting. Check "Coached before" and, on lacrosse events, the Verified badge before approving someone you don't recognize. Confusing "request" with "granted." A team the coach asked for is still just a request until you check it. Pending requests aren't access. Looking for a delete button. Declining a coach isn't an action — a coach with no granted teams already has no access. Unchecking their teams is all it takes.

Which jobs are included if I leave the job filter empty? All of your jobs with activity in the selected window. Use the filter only when you want to isolate specific events — say, comparing two tournaments without the leagues mixed in. Revenue looks lower than I expected for a job. Check the window first — revenue lands in the month it was collected , and registrations often pay months before the event runs. Widen the date range before concluding anything. Then check the Player/Team Counts tab: if counts are down too, it's participation, not a reporting gap. What's in Admin Fee Records that the rollup doesn't show? Tip: for year-over-year comparisons, keep the month span identical and change only the year — mismatched windows are the most common cause of "revenue is down" false alarms.

To act on anything, use the menus to open the specific tool — registrations, scheduling, communications, and so on. Can I change what appears on my Dashboard? Yes. Open customize from the header menu to show or hide individual widgets and reorder them. Save when you're done, and your layout sticks the next time you log in. I hid a widget by mistake — how do I get it back? Reopen customize and toggle it visible again, or use reset to defaults to restore the original layout in one step. Rearranging or hiding widgets changes only your view — everyone else keeps their own. Why do the numbers change when I switch events? As activity picks up, the tiles fill in. Tip: pin the two or three numbers you check most often to the top and hide the rest. A lean Dashboard you actually read beats a crowded one you skim past.

docs.title: Discount Codes
headings: Discount Codes
A registrant says the code isn't working. What do I check?
Does "10" mean 10% off or $10 off?
Why can't I delete a code?
How do I turn off all discounts after a deadline?
How do I know how many times a code has been used?
Can I schedule a code to start and stop on its own?
docs.text: Discount Codes A code only works when it's active AND inside its date window. That's the first thing to check when a registrant says their code was rejected. A registrant says the code isn't working. What do I check? Three things: is the code Active , is today inside its Start–End window, and did they type the Code Name exactly? An inactive or expired code — or a typo — is the usual cause. Does "10" mean 10% off or $10 off? It depends on the Discount Type . As a Percent code, 10 = 10% off; as an Amount code, 10 = $10 off. Set the type deliberately — on higher-priced registrations the two are very different. Why can't I delete a code? Because it's already been used — its Usage Count is above zero, and deleting it would remove part of the payment record. Turn its Active switch off instead; it stops working immediately but the history stays intact. Only unused codes can be deleted. How do I turn off all discounts after a deadline? Use deactivate all to switch every code off in one action. Going the other way, activate all turns them back on — useful for opening a promo window. You can still toggle individual codes from their rows. How do I know how many times a code has been used? The Usage Count column tracks redemptions per code. It's read-only — it reflects real checkouts — and it's what determines whether a code can be deleted or only deactivated. Can I schedule a code to start and stop on its own? Yes — that's what Start Date and End Date are for. Set an early-bird code to begin and end on specific days and, as long as it's active, it turns itself on and off with the window. Tip: always give a promo code an End Date . A discount left active by accident quietly reduces every registration that follows — an end date closes that gap for you.

docs.text: Discount Codes Create the codes registrants type in at checkout to take money off their registration. This screen lists every code for the event; add new ones, edit them, and switch them on or off. Because codes touch what people actually pay, a few details are worth getting right. What a code is made of Code Name — what the registrant types (e.g. SUMMER2026 ). Keep it short and easy to share. Discount Type — how the reduction is calculated: Percent A share of the price — "10" means 10% off. Amount A flat sum — "10" means $10 off. Start / End Date — the window the code is valid. Active — the on/off switch. A code only works when it's active and inside its date window. Percent vs. Amount is the easy one to get wrong. "10" as a Percent is a 10% discount; "10" as an Amount is $10 off. On a $300 registration that's a $30 difference per registrant. Usage and deleting The Usage Count column shows how many times a code has been redeemed. Once a code has been used, you can't delete it — that would erase part of the money record. Instead, switch it off by turning Active to inactive (or letting its End Date pass). Unused codes can be deleted outright. Activate / deactivate in bulk The activate all / deactivate all controls flip every code at once — handy for opening a promo window or shutting all discounts off after a deadline without toggling each row. Common mistakes Leaving a code live too long. A forgotten active code keeps discounting registrations. Set an End Date so it retires itself. Wrong discount type. Double-check Percent vs Amount before saving — it's the difference between 10% and $10. Trying to delete a used code. You can't; deactivate it instead so the redemption history stays intact.

docs.title: Check My Email
headings: Check My Email
Why was my address blocked in the first place?
I removed the block — will I get the emails I missed?
The test send says it succeeded but nothing arrived.
Why is the Send Test button briefly disabled after I use it?
The history doesn't show an email my program says they sent.
docs.text: Check My Email This page covers your own account's addresses. The addresses checked here come from your family and player profile. To check a different address, add it to your profile first. Why was my address blocked in the first place? The two usual causes: a message to you bounced (your mailbox was full, or the address had a typo or didn't exist at the time), or a message was reported as spam from your mailbox — sometimes by an overzealous filter rather than a person. Either way, the email service protects itself by pausing all delivery to that address until the block is removed. I removed the block — will I get the emails I missed? No — messages skipped while blocked aren't re-sent automatically. Check the E-Mail History tab to read anything you missed; new messages will arrive normally from now on. The test send says it succeeded but nothing arrived. That means our service dispatched it and your provider accepted it — so it's landing somewhere in your mailbox. Check spam/junk and promotions , search for "teamsportsinfo", and add the sender to your contacts so future mail goes to your inbox. Why is the Send Test button briefly disabled after I use it? There's a short cooldown between test sends to each address. Wait a minute and it re-enables — one test at a time is all a diagnosis needs anyway. The history doesn't show an email my program says they sent. This page shows emails sent to your addresses for this program . If the message went to a different family member's address, sign in as that member — or ask your program director, who can see the full send log for the event. Tip: adding the sender address to your contacts is the single most effective way to keep program emails out of spam — mail providers rarely filter a known contact.

docs.text: Check My Email Wondering why you haven't received emails from your program? This page shows whether our email service can deliver to the addresses on your account, lets you fix a blocked address yourself, and lists the emails already sent to you — so you can see exactly what went out and when. Current Status tab Every email address on your account is checked and shown with a status pill: OK (we can deliver), Blocked (our email service has stopped sending to it), or Unknown . A blocked address shows when and why it was blocked — usually a bounced message or a spam report from your mail provider. Blocked? Click the fix button to remove the block. Delivery resumes immediately. Use Send test to have a real test message sent to an address — then check your inbox (and spam folder) to confirm it arrives. Blocked addresses hear nothing at all. When an address is blocked, messages aren't delayed — they're skipped entirely, with no bounce or error. If you've had total silence from your program, this is the first thing to check. E-Mail History tab A list of the emails this program has sent to your addresses — subject, recipient, and date. Open a row to read the actual message that was sent. If a message appears here but never reached your inbox, look in your spam/junk folder and add the sender to your contacts. If mail still doesn't arrive Status is OK, the test send succeeded, and you've checked spam — but still nothing? Contact support@teamsportsinfo.com and mention what this page showed; that detail speeds things up considerably.

docs.text: Email Log This log is proof of send, not proof of delivery. A row here means the system dispatched the message to those addresses. Whether an individual mailbox accepted it (vs. spam-filtered or bounced) is a separate deliverability question. Did my message actually send? If it appears in this log with a Sent time, yes — the system dispatched it. The log is newest-first, so a message you just sent shows at the top. Who received a particular email? Open the row. The detail view lists every recipient the message was addressed to, so you can confirm the right people were included. Someone says they never got it — what do I check? First confirm they're in the recipient list for that message (open the row). If they are, the email left the system, and a missing message is usually on the recipient's side — spam/junk folder, a full or mistyped mailbox, or their provider filtering it. The log can't force a redelivery. Can I send or resend a message from here? No — the Email Log is read-only. To send something new, use Bulletins for on-page announcements or the batch-email tools for direct mail. How far back does the log go? It holds the emails sent for this event. Scroll or sort by the Sent time to reach older messages; the most recent are always at the top. Tip: before re-sending an announcement "because no one replied," check the log first — it's common to find the message already went out to everyone, and a duplicate blast just annoys recipients.

docs.text: Email Log A record of every email your event has sent — bulletins, batch messages, notifications. Use it to confirm a message actually went out, see who received it, and check when. It's your answer to "did that email send?" Reading the log The grid lists sent emails newest first, with Subject , Sender , Recipients , and the Sent time. Sort or scan to find the message you're checking on. Open a row to see its full recipient list — every address the message went to — which you can copy if you need it. This is the "it did send" record. If a message is in the log with a sent time and the right recipients, the system dispatched it. What it doesn't do The Email Log shows sent mail ; it doesn't compose or resend. To send a new message, use Bulletins (for on-page announcements) or the batch-email tools; to see why a specific address didn't receive one, that's a deliverability question beyond this list. "When was the last message sent?" — it's at the top; the log is newest-first.

docs.title: E-Mail Troubleshooter
headings: E-Mail Troubleshooter
What does "Suppressed" actually mean?
Is it safe to remove an address from suppression?
The Investigate test says "Recipient side" but they still see nothing. Now what?
Why include my own address in an Investigate run?
Does the Investigate test send a real email?
How is this different from the Email Log?
docs.text: E-Mail Troubleshooter Two tabs, two questions. Suppression List asks "is this address blocked?" Investigate asks "we sent a real test — did it get through, and if not, whose side failed?" What does "Suppressed" actually mean? The email provider (Amazon SES) has this address on its do-not-send list, usually because a past message hard-bounced (mailbox didn't exist) or the recipient marked one as spam. While suppressed, the address receives nothing — and no error is shown anywhere, which is why it looks like silence. Is it safe to remove an address from suppression? Yes, when the person is asking for their mail — that's exactly what removal is for (a fixed mailbox, a mistaken spam click). If the address is genuinely dead, the next send will bounce and it will simply end up suppressed again; no harm done. The Investigate test says "Recipient side" but they still see nothing. Now what? The message left our system and their provider accepted it. Have them check spam/junk and promotions folders, search for the sender address, and add it to their contacts/safe list. School and workplace domains sometimes quarantine mail before the inbox — their IT can release it. Why include my own address in an Investigate run? It's a control. If your copy arrives and the suspect address's doesn't, you've proven the sending side works and isolated the problem to their mailbox — a much stronger answer than "we sent it, trust us." Does the Investigate test send a real email? Yes — a short, clearly-labeled test message is actually dispatched to each address you enter. Warn the person to expect it so they can confirm arrival (or check spam for it). How is this different from the Email Log? The Email Log is history — proof of what was sent and to whom. The Troubleshooter is diagnosis — live checks against the email provider right now. Use the log to confirm a past send; use this tool to find out why the next one won't arrive. Tip: players can self-serve this. The Check My Email page (avatar menu) lets a family check and un-block their own addresses without contacting you.

docs.title: E-Mail Troubleshooter
headings: E-Mail Troubleshooter
Suppression List tab
Investigate E-Mail Failure tab
A practical workflow
docs.text: E-Mail Troubleshooter Your tool for "I never got your email" reports. It answers the two questions that matter: is this address blocked by the email provider, and if not, whose side is the failure on — ours or the recipient's? Suppression List tab Enter one or more addresses (separate with semicolons) and click Check Suppression . Each address comes back Suppressed or Not suppressed . Suppressed means the email provider (Amazon SES) has stopped sending to it — usually after a hard bounce or a spam complaint — along with the reason and the date it happened. Click Remove from suppression to un-stick the address. Future sends resume immediately. Suppression is the #1 cause of "silent" non-delivery. A suppressed address gets nothing — no bounce notice, no error — the system simply skips it. If someone says they've received nothing for weeks, check here first. Investigate E-Mail Failure tab Sends a real test message to each address you enter, then reports the outcome. Each address gets a verdict: Recipient side (we dispatched it fine — the problem is their spam folder, mailbox, or provider), Our side (our sending path rejected it), or Inconclusive . Include a known-good control address — your own inbox — alongside the suspect one. If the control arrives and the suspect doesn't, that's a clean recipient-side diagnosis you can relay with confidence. A practical workflow Parent reports missing email → check Suppression → if suppressed, remove and tell them it's fixed. Not suppressed → run Investigate with their address + your control. Recipient-side verdict → have them check spam/junk and safelist the sender; the system is doing its job.

docs.title: Manage Fields
headings: Manage Fields
What's the difference between the two panels?
Why won't a field let me remove it?
Can I assign several fields at once?
Where do the address and directions show up?
Is this the same as Assign Timeslots?
docs.text: Manage Fields A field must be in the League-Season panel to get games. Assign every field you'll play on before building the schedule — the scheduler ignores anything still in the Available pool. What's the difference between the two panels? Available Fields is the shared pool of fields not yet in this event. League-Season Fields is the set active for this event's scheduling. Move a field from Available to League-Season to put it in play. Why won't a field let me remove it? It already has scheduled games on it — removing it would strand them. Move or clear those games first (in the Rescheduler or by rebuilding), then remove the field. Can I assign several fields at once? Yes — select multiple in the Available panel and assign them as a batch. The filter box and sortable columns help you pick the right ones from a large pool. Where do the address and directions show up? On the schedules families use to find the field. Open a field to set its name, address, map coordinates, and driving directions — complete details here prevent game-day "where is this field?" calls. Is this the same as Assign Timeslots? No — they're two steps of the same job. This screen decides which fields the event has at all, and holds each field's address, coordinates, and directions. Assign Timeslots then decides which of those fields each age group's pools actually play on, and when. So a field has to be in League-Season here before timeslots can be put on it there — which is why this is step 0 of the checklist and timeslots come later. Tip: assign fields before you set up timeslots. Timeslot setup can only offer fields the event already has, so a field added late means going back and re-saving the days it should be on.

docs.text: Manage Fields Pick which fields this event plays on. Fields live in a shared pool; here you pull the ones you're using into the event so scheduling can put games on them. Two side-by-side panels: Available Fields (in the pool, not yet in this event) and League-Season Fields (active for this event's scheduling). This is step 0 of the Scheduling Checklist — the prerequisite, because timeslots are built on fields. The arrow beside the title takes you back to the checklist. Only assigned fields get games. docs.title: Clone Job
headings: Clone Job
Which job gets cloned?
Why didn't my teams come across?
Where is last season's waitlist?
The pools all say "Unassigned" on the new job.
The new job's banner still shows last season's dates.
I cloned to a different customer. Anything special to check?
Is the new site visible to the public before I'm ready?
The event-end warning says the job will be "concluded". What does that mean?
Should I turn on the season roll-forward?
Why is the Clone button disabled?
Where are my discount codes?
I made a practice clone. Can I delete it?
docs.text: Clone Job A clone never arrives live. Registration links closed, bulletins inactive, administrators deactivated — always, regardless of how the source job was set. That's deliberate: you verify the new job first, then turn things on. Which job gets cloned? The job you're currently in — its name and path are shown under the page title. To clone a different job, switch into it first, then come back to this screen. Why didn't my teams come across? Two possibilities. If you picked Leagues, age groups and pools — no teams , that's by design: clubs re-register their teams each season. If you picked the option with teams , only the house teams your organization created and still owns are copied — teams belonging to outside clubs are never cloned, and neither are competing, waitlisted/dropped, or inactive teams. The Teams line in the Plan panel shows exactly how many clone and how many are excluded, and why. Where is last season's waitlist? Waitlists are never cloned. They're generated automatically on the new job, for all job types, whenever an age group's Max number is exceeded — so the new season's waitlist reflects the new season's registrations, not last year's. The pools all say "Unassigned" on the new job. You chose Start fresh for pools — named pools were dropped and every age group got a single Unassigned pool, with any copied teams parked in it. That's the intended workflow: re-pool from scratch once registration closes. If you wanted last season's pool names back, they were an option at clone time ( Keep last season's pools ); on the new job you can simply recreate them on the pool-assignment screen. The new job's banner still shows last season's dates. The clone carried the source banner as-is — the Start on a plain banner option wasn't checked. Fix it on the new job under Configure → Job → Branding : upload this season's artwork, or edit the headline and caption. The banner preview on this screen exists precisely so you catch this before cloning. I cloned to a different customer. Anything special to check? Two things. Payments on the new job bill to the new customer's merchant account — that's what the cross-customer warning is about. And the header logo carried over from the previous owner and shows on every page — replace it under Configure → Job → Branding before the site goes public. Is the new site visible to the public before I'm ready? The new job doesn't appear in the public job listing, but its own pages are reachable at its web address the moment the clone commits. The real protection is the safe state: registration is closed and cloned administrators are inactive, so nobody can sign up or change anything. Finish your setup, then open registration under Configure → Quick Links. The event-end warning says the job will be "concluded". What does that mean? A job whose event end date is in the past reads as over, and a concluded job shows no registration links on its public site — whatever toggles you turn on. Shifted forward from an older event, the end date can land in the past without you noticing; set it to this season's actual end date before cloning. Should I turn on the season roll-forward? Rolling into a new season — yes: years in names and text advance one, and birth-date/graduation ranges shift with them. Building a second job for the same season — no: there's nothing to advance, and the plan will note the clone stays in the same year. Why is the Clone button disabled? Either something on the form is invalid (a path or name collision, an invalid slug — the field shows the error inline), the affirmation checkbox isn't ticked, or the plan is still refreshing. The clone always runs against the plan you're looking at — if you've just changed a field, wait for the Plan header to read current . Where are my discount codes? Discount codes are never cloned — last season's codes on a new season's prices is a mistake waiting to happen. Add this season's codes on the new job under Configure → Discount Codes . I made a practice clone. Can I delete it? On the development and staging environments, yes — Configure → Job offers a delete for sandbox clones. Production jobs are never deleted. Tip: read the Plan panel like a receipt before you click Clone. The warnings and the per-step counts are the clone telling you, in advance, everything it's about to do — a surprise on the new job means something was visible there first.

docs.text: Clone Job This workbench builds next season's job from the one you're standing in. The left side is the form — what to name the new job, what to copy, what to leave behind. The right side is the live Plan : it recomputes as you type, showing exactly what the clone will create, with counts, warnings, and date shifts. Nothing happens until you check the affirmation and click Clone job . Clones arrive switched off. Every clone lands with registration closed, bulletins inactive, and administrators deactivated — nobody can sign up for, or administer, a job you're still building. The What arrives switched off panel on the form is the checklist of what you turn back on, and where. The form, top to bottom Owner Which customer the new job bills to. Picking a different customer than the source is allowed but flagged — review the plan warnings, and remember the header logo carries over from the old owner. Identity Job path (the URL segment), job name, year, season, display name. Path and name are checked for collisions as you leave the field. Leagues can be renamed inline for the new season. Dates Expiry dates arrive seeded from the source plus one year. Event start/end are for tournaments only — player sites seed team dates automatically. Communications From/CC/BCC addresses, reschedule and always-copy lists, mail-to and pay-to. Pre-filled from the source; emptying a field clears it on the new job. What gets copied The structural choices — league structure, pools, payments, store, season roll-forward, and the home-page banner. Each is covered below. How much of the league structure to copy The one decision that shapes everything else. Three choices: Nothing — start empty. You build leagues, age groups, and pools yourself on the LADT screen. Nobody can register until you do. Leagues, age groups and pools — no teams. Last season's shape carries over, ready for a new season's entries. Clubs re-register their teams every season. …plus your own teams. Everything above, plus the house teams your organization created and still owns. Teams belonging to outside clubs are never copied. Waitlists are never cloned — they regenerate automatically on the new job whenever an age group's Max number is exceeded. When structure is copied you also choose what happens to pools : keep last season's named pools (they arrive empty, ready to re-seed) or start fresh — every age group gets a single Unassigned pool and any copied teams land in it, so you re-pool once registration closes. Money and store Payment methods start matching the source — credit card only, credit card or check, or check only. Changeable here or later on Configure → Job → Payment. eCheck defaults to off — the safe choice until the new season's bank details are confirmed. It has no effect on a card-only job. Online store can start off or match the source, but merchandise and inventory are never copied — a store switched on here opens empty. Season roll-forward When on, any four-digit year in age-group names, team names, bulletins, and page text advances one year — "Boys 2026" becomes "Boys 2027" — and birth-date and graduation-year ranges shift to match, so a U10 age group still describes U10s next season. Turn it off when you're building a second job for the same season. Home page banner and logo The preview shows exactly how the new site will open. Start on a plain banner drops last season's overlay artwork, headline, and caption — nothing stale can show — while keeping the background photo for when you re-upload this season's artwork under Configure → Job → Branding . Leave it unchecked and the source banner carries over as-is; the headline and caption are editable right here before the clone runs. The header logo always carries over and shows on every page. If the artwork names a season — or the clone changed owners — replace it under Branding before the site goes public. The Plan panel The right column is the clone spelled out before it happens: warnings first, then a count for every step (age groups, teams, bulletins, fee modifiers…), the team breakdown (structure teams that clone vs. competing, waitlist/dropped, and inactive teams that don't), the processing-fee rates the new job will use, and any automatic date shifts. Expand the detail sections to see each age group and bulletin by name. The Clone button waits for a current plan — if you've just changed something, let "refreshing…" finish. After the clone You're switched into the new job and land on its home page. Work the What you need to turn on list: open registration links under Configure → Quick Links , activate the administrators you want under Configure → Administrators , review and activate bulletins, re-add discount codes, and set roster visibility. Registration stays closed until you open it — verify everything first.
