docs.text: Team Roster — questions Everyone on the team can see this roster. The cards — names, phone numbers, emails, and parent contacts — are visible to every player, parent, and coach on the team. Treat it as a shared team directory. Who can see my phone number and email? Everyone on your team's roster — players, parents, and coaches. The roster is a shared directory so teammates can reach one another. If something shouldn't be shown, update it on your account or ask the event organizer. What are "Contact 1" and "Contact 2"? They're the parents or guardians on a player's account — the family contacts we have on file. Each one's email and phone are listed in full, so you can read, copy, or tap them to get in touch. Cards with no family on file simply leave this section out. How do I email the whole team, or just a few people? For everyone, use Email All . For a few, tick the checkbox on the cards you want and choose Email Selected . Each person receives your message individually, so replies come back only to you. A teammate's email or phone is blank or wrong. The roster shows what's on each person's registration — blank means it isn't on file. Update your own details on your account; for someone else's, the player or parent updates their own, or the event organizer can help. Why don't some cards show a uniform number or position? Those appear only once they've been assigned. A missing number or position simply hasn't been set on that registration yet. Can players see the roster, or only coaches? Both — it's a directory for everyone on the team. Coaches and staff are marked with a badge; everyone else is a player. The page says the roster isn't available. The event organizer decides when team rosters are visible, and the setting can differ for players and coaches. If it's off, check back later or ask the organizer to turn it on. I'm not on a team yet — where's my roster? Your roster appears once you've been placed on a team; until then there's nothing to show. Placement is handled by your club or the event organizer. Tip: tap a person's email or phone — or a parent's — to reach them in one step from your device.

docs.text: View Schedule Missing games? A filter is almost always the reason. Check the filter chips at the top and clear the ones you don't want — that's the fix for "where did my games go?" How do I enter or fix a score? On the Games tab, enter the score right on the game as an admin. Standings and brackets recalculate from it. To change more than the score, open the game and edit its details. What's the fastest way to find games that still need scores? Turn on the Unscored filter — it hides everything that already has a result, leaving just the games you still need to enter. Work straight down that list at the end of a round. What's the difference between filtering By Club and By League? Two paths to the same games. By Club drills Club → Age Group → Division → Team — handy when a club asks about their schedule. By League drills the event's own League → Age Group → Division → Team structure. Use whichever matches how you're thinking about the games. My standings look wrong. What should I check? Standings are computed entirely from entered scores, so a missing or mistyped score is the usual culprit. Use the Unscored filter to spot games without a result, and re-check any score that looks off on the Games tab. How do I move a game to a different time or field? Not here — this screen records results and edits game details. To relocate a game to another timeslot or field, use the Rescheduler , which is built for moving games (including weather shifts). Is this the same schedule the public sees? Yes — it's the same games and standings, published on the public schedule page. The difference is that as an admin you also get score entry and game editing; the public view is read-only. Tip: keep scores current during the event. Because standings and brackets are computed live from them, entering results as games finish means seeding and playoff pictures are always right — no end-of-day catch-up scramble.

docs.text: View Schedule This is the admin's window into the whole event's games — browse the schedule, check standings and brackets, find team contacts, and (as an admin) enter or fix scores. It's the same schedule the public sees, plus the editing tools only you get. Listed as Schedule Viewer under Tools on the Scheduling Checklist — it unlocks once games exist. The arrow beside the title takes you back. Four tabs Games Every scheduled game. Enter or edit scores here, and open a game to adjust its details. Standings Pool standings, updated from the scores you enter — the source for bracket seeding. Brackets Playoff brackets as they fill in from results. Contacts Team contacts, for when you need to reach a coach or club rep. Narrowing the list with filters A full event has hundreds of games, so filtering is how you get to the ones you want. You can filter two ways: By Club Drill Club → Age Group → Division → Team — best when you're looking at one club's games. By League Drill League → Age Group → Division → Team — best for working within the event's structure. Add day, time, and field filters, or flip on Unscored to show only games still missing a result. Each filter you pick becomes a removable chip, so you can always see what's applied and clear it. Entering scores (admin) On the Games tab, enter a game's score directly — standings and brackets update from it. Use the Unscored filter to work through exactly the games that still need results — faster than hunting for gaps. Open a game to edit fuller details or run the game clock where that's in play. Common mistakes Not seeing games you expect. A filter is probably still applied — check the chips and clear the ones you don't want. Wondering why standings look off. Standings are computed from entered scores; a missing or wrong score is usually the cause. The Unscored filter finds the gaps. Confusing this with the Rescheduler. Here you record results and tweak game details; to move a game to a different field or time, use the Rescheduler .

docs.text: Widget Editor One event, or every event? That's the question behind almost everything on this screen. Job Overrides changes one event. Default Matrix and Role Assignments change every event of a job type. How do I tell whether a widget is switched on for the event I'm in? The In Use column on Widget Definitions tells you how many events have it, but not which ones. For a definite answer about the event you're in, click the green job count — or open Job Overrides , which starts on your current event — and look at that widget's row. How do I remove a widget from one event? In Job Overrides , use the at the end of that widget's row, then Save Overrides . You can also right-click an individual checkbox to undo just that one role. Unticking a box is not the same thing. That records "switched off for this event" and keeps the row. Both hide the widget; the row button leaves things cleaner. I added one widget and the rest of the Dashboard changed. Why? An event with no widgets assigned shows a standard Dashboard — banner and bulletins. The moment it has even one assignment, it switches to showing exactly what's assigned , and the standard layout stops applying. If you want the old panels back alongside your new widget, assign them explicitly too. What does "Not in use" mean? Is it broken? No. It means the widget is defined but no event and no automatic rule uses it, so nobody currently sees it. That's normal for something just built and not yet rolled out. There's a warning about a widget not being set up. What is it telling me? A developer has built that widget, but it has no definition here — so it can't be added to any event yet. Click it to create the definition, which opens the Add Widget form already filled in. Don't treat it as a to-do list. If you're not sure a widget is wanted, leave it. Setting up something that was replaced by a newer panel just puts a duplicate on the page. Why can't I delete a widget? Because something still uses it. Clear its assignments first — the automatic rules in Default Matrix and any per-event entries in Job Overrides — then delete it. The In Use column shows you what's holding it. What is the Component Key, and what happens if I invent one? It's the link between this definition and the code a developer wrote. Pick from the list and it's guaranteed to match. If you type a custom key with no matching code, the widget saves without complaint and then renders as blank space on every event you add it to. There's no error — just an empty gap. Only use a custom key when a developer has told you the name to use. What's the difference between Role Assignments and Job Overrides? Role Assignments (inside the Add/Edit Widget dialog) creates automatic rules. Tick a job type there and every event of that type gets the widget — existing and future. Job Overrides changes one event only. If you meant "just this one tournament," that's the tab you want. Can a Director change their own widgets? They can show, hide, and reorder widgets on their own Dashboard through customize — that's personal to their login and doesn't affect anyone else. They cannot add or remove widgets from the event. This screen is SuperUser only. What does the drag handle do? It sets the order widgets appear in on the Dashboard, within their category. Drag a row up or down, then Save Overrides . Does any of this affect the public event page? Not currently. Widgets in the public workspace can be defined and assigned, but the public page shows its banner and bulletins from a fixed layout rather than from these settings. Switching a public widget off here will not change what visitors see.

docs.text: Widget Editor Widgets are the panels and tiles that make up a Dashboard. This screen is where you decide which widgets exist, which kinds of events get them automatically, and which individual events get something different. A widget needs two things to appear. A developer has to build it, and you have to set it up here. Building it alone does nothing — it stays invisible until it has a definition on this screen and is assigned to an event. The three tabs Widget Definitions — the catalog of every widget that exists, with its name, category, and where it's currently deployed. Add, edit, and delete widgets here. Job Overrides — what one specific event gets. Add a widget to just this event, or switch off one it would otherwise inherit. Default Matrix — the automatic rules. Anything ticked here is given to every event of that type, for the roles you choose. Reading the "In Use" column The Definitions tab tells you where each widget has actually landed: 3 jobs — attached to three specific events. Click it to open Job Overrides. auto · 7 — an automatic rule gives it to seven job types, no per-event setup needed. Not in use — defined, but nobody sees it. Usually means it's built and waiting. Turning a widget on for one event Open Job Overrides . It opens on the event you're currently in. Expand the workspace and find the widget's row. Tick the box under each role that should see it. Save Overrides . Turning it back off Use the at the end of the widget's row, then save. The button tells you which it will do: Remove from this job — you added it here, so it goes away cleanly. Revert to inherited — an automatic rule supplies it, so the row returns to that rule. The row button only appears when the row actually differs from what the event would inherit. Role Assignments in the widget dialog reach every event. The Role Assignments section inside Add/Edit Widget writes automatic rules — it applies to every event of the job types you tick , not the one you're looking at. To change a single event, use Job Overrides. Colours in the override matrix Inherited — comes from an automatic rule; you haven't touched it. Override (enabled) — you switched on something this event wouldn't normally get. Override (disabled) — you switched off something it would normally get. Job-specific addition — added for this event only, with no rule behind it. Good to know This screen is SuperUser only . Directors can arrange their own Dashboard, but cannot add or remove widgets. Attaching the first widget to an event replaces its default Dashboard layout — see the FAQ. Changes are held until you Save ; leaving with unsaved edits will warn you first.
